review.nature: separate automated adversarial review; NOT production acceptance, NOT security certification, NOT visual/audio quality approval

scope_notes: No production file, original six spec, or prior evidence byte was modified (see INTEGRITY in REPORT.md).
Only synthetic technical fixtures in temporary directories; no real ffmpeg run, no media generated, no network.
Known AAC zero-vs-absent summary defect and the CPU/memory cap gap belong to the other session and were not rediscovered or fixed here.

severity_scale.MEDIUM: wrong or misleading truthful-status/qualification behaviour on an advertised guarantee, no data loss
severity_scale.LOW: contract slip, robustness or narrow-domain defect; conservative failure mode

validated_defects.title: SIGTERM/SIGINT outside the mux/render step is swallowed by run_bounded; the run is misreported and keeps launching child processes
source: tools/video-core/video_core/runner.py:268-270 (KeyboardInterrupt converted into a normal RunResult(outcome=INTERRUPTED))
tools/video-core/video_core/tools.py:98-100 + render.py:74-77 + avmux/mux.py:96-99 (interrupted version probe => 'tool unavailable' => SKIPPED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, exit 3)
tools/video-core/video_core/avmux/mux.py:108-112 (both preflight ffprobe calls always run; INTERRUPTED => ValidationFailed preflight_probe_failed, exit 1)
tools/video-core/video_core/avmux/mux.py:249-253 + 158 and readback.py run_probe (interrupted readback => INSPECTION_FAILED, exit 4)
only the mux/render step itself maps INTERRUPTED: avmux/mux.py:180-184, render.py:155-161
validated_defects.trigger: Owned fake ffmpeg/ffprobe (adv_fake_tools.py) that sleeps 8 s at (a) `ffmpeg -version`, (b) preflight `ffprobe` of the video, (c) the first readback `ffmpeg -f framemd5`; SIGTERM sent to the avmux CLI pid only, after the sleep marker file appears.
validated_defects.command: python3 run_audit.py -v --pattern 'test_adv_lane4_exec.py'   # or: python3 -m unittest test_adv_lane4_exec.InterruptSemantics (ADV_STRICT=1 makes it a hard failure)
validated_defects.expected: exit code 130, status INTERRUPTED, no child process launched after the signal
validated_defects.actual: (a) rc 3 SKIPPED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE ('version probe did not exit cleanly: INTERRUPTED'), 1 further child launched; (b) rc 1 rejection preflight_probe_failed, 1 further child launched (the audio probe); (c) rc 4, on-disk receipt INSPECTION_FAILED, 1 further child launched (output decode)
validated_defects.consequence: A cancellation is reported as 'tool unavailable', 'input invalid' or 'readback failed'; automation that branches on exit codes 1/3/4 will treat a user cancel as a technical outcome, and processes keep being started after the cancel. Same pattern in the video `render` command (render.py:70-77).
validated_defects.severity_rationale: Truthful-status defect on an advertised guarantee ('record phase/exit/signal/timeout/drain separately', 130 = interrupted) that affects every stage except the mux step; not data-destructive; no wrong media.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: Minimal: add `def raise_if_interrupted(res): if res.outcome == INTERRUPTED: raise KeyboardInterrupt` to runner.py and call it right after every run_bounded in tools.probe_version/_listing, readback.run_probe, avmux/mux.py:_probe/_hash_text/_run and render.py; add `except KeyboardInterrupt: receipt['status']=STATUS_INTERRUPTED` beside the existing `except Exception` in render() and mux() (audiomix/mix.py:179-180 is the model). The existing INTERRUPTED mapping of the mux/render step stays.
validated_defects.platform: Linux x86_64 only; Windows not run

validated_defects.title: A caller-chosen root whose path contains a non-UTF-8 byte strands an IN_PROGRESS receipt after the run (video render) or after creating the run directory (avmux)
source: tools/video-core/video_core/receipt.py:47-48 (json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8') is strict)
tools/video-core/video_core/paths.py:113-123 (real_directory accepts a name that cannot be encoded)
tools/video-core/video_core/render.py:95-114 (final receipt carries argv with the run directory; encode error escapes after output.mp4 was promoted)
tools/video-core/video_core/avmux/mux.py:123-137 (run directory created, first receipt already contains the asset root through the preflight probe argv)
validated_defects.trigger: Directory named b'out_caf\xe9' (valid on Linux; Python str '\udce9'); video render with the owned fake tools, and avmux mux with an assets directory named b'assets_caf\xe9'.
validated_defects.expected: either refuse the root before anything is created, or finish with a terminal receipt
validated_defects.actual: video: UnicodeEncodeError escapes render(); output.mp4 exists; receipt.json still says IN_PROGRESS/stage render. avmux: UnicodeEncodeError; run directory exists and is empty (no receipt).
validated_defects.consequence: Caller gets an exception instead of a receipt although a render completed; the only record says IN_PROGRESS (= UNKNOWN by documented convention, so the failure is conservative, but it contradicts 'raises before anything is created' and strands a promoted output).
validated_defects.severity_rationale: Rare precondition (raw non-UTF-8 directory name, Linux); failure mode is conservative (IN_PROGRESS means UNKNOWN); no wrong media or hash.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: In paths.real_directory add `try: real.encode('utf-8') except UnicodeEncodeError: raise UnsafePath(... 'root_invalid')` (rejects before any side effect). Defence in depth: receipt.dumps(...).encode('utf-8','backslashreplace').
validated_defects.platform: Linux (raw bytes in names). macOS/Windows not applicable or not run

validated_defects.title: After an unexpected exception the receipt inventories no outputs, records no sha256_after, and (avmux/render) leaves tmp/ undocumented, although the partial files exist
source: tools/video-core/video_core/audiomix/mix.py:181-183 (handler) vs 230 (outputs only set on the normal path), 233-238 (sha256_after only on the normal path)
tools/video-core/video_core/avmux/mux.py:140-142 vs 220-224 (outputs, tmp cleanup)
tools/video-core/video_core/render.py:110-112 vs 195-211
validated_defects.trigger: An input file vanishes while the run is in progress: audiomix (asset removed by the cancel hook before chunk 2), avmux (owned fake ffmpeg removes the WAV during the mux).
validated_defects.expected: status UNKNOWN (correct) AND outputs[] listing stem.wav.partial/output.mov.partial/plan.canonical.json/ffprobe.output.json, inputs with sha256_after (null if unreadable), tmp_cleanup stated
validated_defects.actual: status UNKNOWN + internal_error (correct), but outputs == [], no sha256_after, no tmp_cleanup; avmux leaves tmp/ and ffprobe.output.json unlisted
validated_defects.consequence: The one document that is supposed to describe a run that went wrong omits the evidence that exists next to it; a reader who trusts the receipt would not know a partial output is there.
validated_defects.severity_rationale: Status is already conservative (UNKNOWN); only the inventory is incomplete.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: Move the inventory/hash/cleanup block of each _run into a helper `finalize(run_dir, receipt)` that is also called (best-effort, in its own try) from the `except` handler in mix()/mux()/render().
validated_defects.overlap_with_other_session: none (the other session fixes AAC zero-vs-absent summaries and the OPTIONAL resource envelope)

validated_defects.title: avmux plan: a malformed audio receipt raises AttributeError/RecursionError instead of a typed rejection
source: tools/video-core/video_core/avmux/plan.py:100-113 (json.loads without type checks; .get() on whatever was decoded)
validated_defects.trigger: Receipt file (hash pinned in the manifest) whose JSON is `[]`, `null`, `"x"`, `1`, or {status MIXED_VERIFIED, outputs:"x"}, outputs:[1], readback.wav:"x", or 100000 nested arrays.
validated_defects.command: python3 -m unittest test_adv_lane1_parsers.AudioReceiptInput  (exploratory origin: probes/p3.py); CLI: python3 -m video_core.avmux plan MANIFEST --asset-root ROOT => traceback, exit 1, empty stdout
validated_defects.expected: ValidationFailed/UnsafePath with an audio_receipt_* issue code (exit 1 with the structured error)
validated_defects.actual: AttributeError ('list'/'NoneType'/'str'/'int' object has no attribute 'get'); RecursionError for deep nesting
validated_defects.consequence: Untyped crash from untrusted-ish input at plan time; callers that catch VideoCoreError (as the CLIs do) get a traceback.
validated_defects.severity_rationale: Plan-time robustness; no side effects occur; input must be a file the caller pinned by SHA-256.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: Reuse the strict loader: `rec = parse_json_bytes(raw, limits)`; then `if not isinstance(rec, dict) ... outputs must be a list of objects ... readback.wav must be an object` each raising audio_receipt_unreadable/_shape; catch RecursionError (parse_json_bytes already does).

validated_defects.title: avmux 'qualification' by an audio receipt checks three fields only: a hand-written or internally inconsistent receipt qualifies the stem
source: tools/video-core/video_core/avmux/plan.py:105-112 (status == MIXED_VERIFIED, one outputs[role=stem].sha256, readback.wav.sample_count)
validated_defects.trigger: Receipts with only {status, outputs:[{role:stem,sha256}], readback:{wav:{sample_count}}} (3 fields); with readback.all_ok=false; with outputs[stem].partial=true; with quality_evaluated=true; with duplicate `status` keys (last wins: HOLD then MIXED_VERIFIED); with sample_count 4800.0 (float).
validated_defects.expected: documented contract: receipt must be an audio-planner receipt for exactly this stem; internally inconsistent or schema-less receipts refused
validated_defects.actual: all of the above are accepted and recorded as `status: MIXED_VERIFIED` in the avmux plan/receipt (plan_sha256 None)
validated_defects.consequence: Any adopter who reads `audio.receipt.status == MIXED_VERIFIED` in the avmux plan as machine-checked qualification is trusting a caller-authored JSON; inconsistent combinations (all_ok=false + MIXED_VERIFIED) that the audio planner never emits are accepted.
validated_defects.severity_rationale: The feature exists to qualify stems; the weak check can mislead an adopter although nothing in the docs claims authentication. Because receipts are inherently unauthenticated, the minimum is consistency + a clear statement.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: Require schema == 'video_core.audio_receipt/1', written is True, stage == 'complete', readback.all_ok is True, every readback check ok, stem entry partial is False, quality_evaluated is False, sample_count `type is int`, 64-hex plan_sha256 present; parse with the strict duplicate-key-rejecting loader; copy warnings/coverage.gap_count into the avmux plan (see O-1); state in AVMUX_SPEC that the receipt is a pinned but unauthenticated caller file.
validated_defects.overlap_with_other_session: none (other session: AAC receipt accuracy of the avmux OUTPUT receipt, not this INPUT receipt qualification)

validated_defects.title: Drain-limit breach is classified FLOOD_KILLED or EXITED_ZERO/ok depending on a 50 ms polling race
source: tools/video-core/video_core/runner.py:254-267 (flood flag only consulted while the child is still running)
tools/video-core/video_core/runner.py:171 (flag set by the drain thread)
validated_defects.trigger: Child writes 2 MB to stdout and exits at once with max_drain_bytes=1000; control: same child lingers 1 s.
validated_defects.command: python3 -m unittest test_adv_lane4_exec.RunnerDefects.test_output_beyond_the_drain_limit_is_never_reported_as_a_clean_exit (ADV_STRICT=1 for a hard failure)
validated_defects.expected: the documented bound ('child output beyond this => killed') is visible in the outcome either way
validated_defects.actual: quick child: EXITED_ZERO, ok=True, 2000000 bytes captured/hashed; lingering child: FLOOD_KILLED
validated_defects.consequence: Bounded-diagnostics receipts can report a clean exit for an output stream that exceeded the configured bound (mostly cosmetic for ffmpeg stderr; relevant for the decoded-PCM drain bound used by the avmux readback).
validated_defects.severity_rationale: Classification race on an edge condition; data is still fully drained and hashed; readbacks have independent size checks.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: After the wait loop: `if state['flood'].is_set() and result.kill_reason is None: result.kill_reason = 'flood'` (classify() then yields FLOOD_KILLED for an already exited child).
validated_defects.reproducibility: racy by construction; quick-exit case reproduced in every run of the matrix
validated_defects.overlap_with_other_session: OPTIONAL resource envelope is a CPU/memory cap; this is the existing byte bound's classification, not a new cap

validated_defects.title: Interrupt (Ctrl-C) during pipe drain escapes run_bounded and leaves a process of the owned group running
source: tools/video-core/video_core/runner.py:272-282 (drain/orphan section is outside the try that handles KeyboardInterrupt, lines 253-270)
validated_defects.trigger: Child exits 0 leaving one self-expiring (5 s) grandchild that holds the pipes; SIGINT delivered 0.6 s after the grandchild exists, i.e. while run_bounded waits (drain_timeout 3 s).
validated_defects.expected: no member of the owned process group survives the unwinding of run_bounded
validated_defects.actual: KeyboardInterrupt escapes; grandchild still alive (the test kills it itself afterwards)
validated_defects.consequence: The 'only owned children, nothing left behind' guarantee has a window; effect bounded by the child's own lifetime.
validated_defects.severity_rationale: Narrow window; needs an orphaned pipe holder and a cancel during drain.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: Wrap lines 272-282 in the same try (or try/finally that calls _signal_group(proc, SIGKILL) when drain is incomplete before re-raising).
validated_defects.reproducibility: deterministic with marker synchronisation (the first matrix run showed an environment-dependent harness defect, see harness_defects H7)

validated_defects.title: numeric.finite_seconds raises OverflowError (not the documented ValueError) for an absurdly large Python int
source: tools/video-core/video_core/numeric.py:54 (`{value:g}` formats an int > 1e308 through float)
validated_defects.actual: OverflowError: int too large to convert to float
validated_defects.consequence: Library callers catching ValueError (as the CLIs do) miss it; CLI flags are float-typed so the CLI path is unaffected (inf is rejected cleanly).
validated_defects.severity_rationale: API-contract slip, no side effect, not reachable from the CLI.
validated_defects.proposed_fix: line 54: `f"{name} must be <= {ceiling:g} seconds (got {_describe(value)})"` (the helper exists on line 21).

validated_defects.title: All three CLIs crash with a traceback (empty stdout) when a rejected input contains a lone-surrogate JSON key
source: tools/video-core/video_core/episode.py:161 and audiomix/manifest.py:88 (issue path embeds the raw key)
tools/video-core/video_core/receipt.py:47-48 (strict UTF-8 encode)
tools/video-core/video_core/cli.py:29-31, audiomix/cli.py:30-32, avmux/cli.py:30-32 (_emit)
validated_defects.trigger: Manifest/episode JSON with an extra key written as "\ud800".
validated_defects.command: python3 -m video_core validate EP.json ; python3 -m video_core.audiomix validate M.json ; python3 -m video_core.avmux validate M.json
validated_defects.expected: exit 1 with a structured {ok:false,error:{...}} document on stdout

validated_defects.title: Audio planner rejects the whole manifest for a zero-sample frame range on an unselected or OMIT event (fps > 48000)

documented_limitations_and_observations.title: Transient swap-and-restore of an audio asset during the mix is undetected and yields MIXED_VERIFIED with inputs_unchanged=true
source: tools/video-core/video_core/audiomix/mix.py:107-109 (asset re-opened and re-parsed for every chunk and event)
tools/video-core/video_core/audiomix/mix.py:233-238 (hash only after the run)
documented_limitations_and_observations.note: Documented as 'race windows' (AUDIO_SPEC.md, LIMITATIONS.md). New information: LIMITATIONS.md describes 'the tiny gap' for FFmpeg's open(); for the mixer the unprotected window is the whole mix. Persistent swaps ARE detected (UNKNOWN). Hardening proposal: open each asset once after hashing, keep the descriptor, and compare fstat(ino,size,mtime_ns) before every chunk (or read the needed PCM range into memory right after the hash).

documented_limitations_and_observations.title: fontcheck scan is O(distinct code points x cmap groups/segments)
source: tools/video-core/video_core/fontcheck.py:85-94, 112-122

Extrapolation only (NOT executed): 5,000 distinct characters x 20,000 groups ~ 43 s; limits-maximum (262,144 x 1,000,000) ~ 31 h of plan-time CPU. Proposal: sort groups once and bisect.

test_harness_defects_found_and_fixed.description: Lane 2 first draft: avmux fixtures named the wav 'a.wav' but the case files wrote 'mono.wav' => every avmux case 'asset_missing' (fixed in the test).
Lane 1: the manifest() builder coerced a string scope into a list, so 'scope: "a"' was never tested (fixed).
Lane 1: the first fps catalogue contained no exact .5 sample boundary (needs 2^8 | n); the test that asserts their presence failed and the catalogue was extended.
Lane 3: argv audio check matched 'a=0' inside the filtergraph; audited-body indentation; asset shorter than the longest span (Rng assertion) (fixed).

Lane 4: fake ffmpeg wrote the partial output after sleeping/failing (real muxers have it earlier); wrong md5 literal in a mutation; incomplete-drain expectation (drain_complete is True after the group kill, orphan_group_killed is the signal) (fixed).

F-RUN-2 harness had a quoting IndentationError that was swallowed as 'expected failure'. Consequence: known_defect now re-reports any non-AssertionError as ERROR and scenario preconditions use harness_check() (HarnessError).

First full matrix: the F-RUN-2 scenario did not run because a background job started with '&' inherits SIGINT=SIG_IGN, so Python never installed its KeyboardInterrupt handler. The HarnessError guard reported 5 ERRORs; fixed by installing default_int_handler in the scenario. Logs kept in logs/attempts/.

unverified_or_out_of_reach: Windows and macOS (nothing run; reparse-point and name-aliasing behaviour is stub/characterisation only)
Real FFmpeg/ffprobe behaviour of the mux, AAC encoder delay, real decoded-frame hashes (no real tool was run on media; the owned fakes emit canned answers and are never mux evidence)
Ceiling-sized inputs (10-minute / 200 M-work audio, 4 GiB sources, 18000-frame decodes)
EACCES/EIO on a readable-looking asset (suite runs as root; static concern: audiomix/plan.py opens the asset outside a try block so an OSError would surface untyped)
audiomix CLI SIGTERM wiring (cancel flag) end to end; only the API-level cancel hook is exercised
Perceptual A/V sync, audio or visual quality, creative selection/voice/timing (explicitly not evaluated)
